# OpenSurfaces.jl

> Julia package for singular integrals on flat open surfaces Ω ⊂ R² (the plane z = 0, with holes and several components) and on their edges Γ = ∂Ω: adaptive high-order boundary panels from a parametrization, area meshes of quadrilateral panels with a graded edge layer whose quadrature weights carry the d^{-1/2} edge singularity of first-kind densities, local quadrature corrections for singular and near-singular targets (area and line sources), fast sums (FMM2D, FMM3D, Ewald + NUFFT, smooth convolution), kernels from Fourier symbols (a standard base kernel plus a remainder tabulated by Hankel transforms), and evaluators built from them. It knows no physical model: kernels are passed in.

Source: not registered; `Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/scottweady/OpenSurfaces.jl")`, Julia ≥ 1.12. Start Julia with threads.

User API: geometry `discretize_curve(γ, p; tol)` (γ 2π-periodic counterclockwise; a hole is `reverse_curve` of one), `discretize_curves`, `build_mesh(panels, p; holes, edge_layers, edge_grading) -> (bd::BoundaryDisc, ad::AreaDisc, info)`, `build_mesh([[outer, holes...], ...], p)` for several drops, `mesh_quality`, `interpolate_nodal`; nodes `ad.x`, weights `ad.w`, `ad.wfac` (μ = μ̃ · wfac on the weighted edge panels), `bd.x`, `bd.w`, `bd.n` (outward), `bd.τ`, `bd.κ`. Evaluator: `E = Evaluator(K, ad; targets = :area | :boundary | points | tuple, bd, density = :stored | :smooth, fast = :auto | :ewald | :fmm | :direct, remainder, tol, eps)`, `E(f)` (scalars or Vec2 per node by `kernel_shape(K)`), `Evaluator(K, bd; targets)` for line sources; as an operator `size`, `eltype`, `mul!`, `*` on interleaved Float64 vectors (Krylov solvers), `evaluator_matrix(E)`, `local_blocks(E, panel_groups(ad))` for block-Jacobi preconditioners. Kernels: `Stokeslet3D(; μ_3D)` (half-space; μ_3D = 2μ_f for an unbounded fluid), `LaplaceKernel3D()`, `LaplaceKernel2D()`, `LaplaceGradient2D()`, `BiharmonicGradient2D(; κ, R)`, `MHKernel(k)`, `MHNormalKernel(k, normals)`, closed forms `G2`, `G3`, `P2`, `T2`, `stress2`; any callable `K(r)` or `K(i, r)` with r = target − source returning a number or a `Mat2` (declare `OpenSurfaces.kernel_shape(::T) = (2, 2)` or `(2, 1)` for non-scalar kernels); `SymbolKernel(symbol; base, scale, outputs, remainder, tol)`. Potentials: `SingleLayer3D(ad; remainder)` with `single_layer`, `VolumePotentials(ad, bd)` with `volume_grad`, `volume_bgrad`, `volume_potential`. Boundary: `LineQuad(bd)`, `slp2d_velocity_matrix`, `traction_self_matrix`, `slp2d_eval`, `line_correction`. Lower level: `area_correction(ad, K; targets, tol)`, `area_local_weights`, `stokes2d_apply`, `stokes3d_plane_apply`, `EwaldStokes3D`, `EwaldLaplace3D`, `RadialEwald2D`, `FilmEwald`, `SmoothConvolution`. Default accuracy `OpenSurfaces.DEFAULT_TOL` = 1e-6.

## Docs

- Home: what it does, one call, what it offers
- Getting started: installation, a mesh (holes, several drops), nodes and the two density forms, an evaluator, the evaluator as an operator (GMRES, block-Jacobi), line sources, kernels of your own, kernels from symbols
- Method: geometry (boundary panels, the edge layer and its weight, graded layers, the interior); quadrature (polar rules on a panel, adaptive near it, log product rules on Γ, the traction); fast sums (FMM normalizations, Ewald + NUFFT, smooth convolution); kernels from Fourier symbols (Hankel tables, conditions on base and remainder); limits
- Examples: scripts that evaluate or solve against exact solutions
- API reference: every exported name
- Code map: which functions each feature runs, and the layout of src/
